UnitStatement: This document defines the DEL-02-05 persistence and deterministic round-trip contract.
The companion schema is schemas/project_persistence.schema.yaml, written as strict JSON syntax so it can be parsed without a YAML dependency.
The persisted project document is a versioned, schema-governed domain artifact.
Public repository fixtures and examples must not contain protected standards text, copied tables, proprietary values, private rule-pack contents, or professional approval claims.

The project document envelope owns persistence metadata: schema version, project identity, migration status, canonical JSON/JCS hash metadata, private-data markers, diagnostics, and round-trip manifest entries.
The actual model payload is delegated to schemas/model.schema.yaml.
The MVP physical project package/container is the SCA-003 local storage profile: a user-chosen, local SQLite-backed project store/index owned by the application-service persistence boundary.
SQLite is the durable local container and query/index substrate; it is not the canonical domain contract.
Canonical JSON/JCS-compatible payload bytes, schema validation, and hash metadata remain the source of truth for domain semantics and interchange.
SQLite tables may hold canonical payload bytes and indexed projections.
SQL DDL, table names, raw SQLite handles, and direct SQL mutation are private implementation details and must not become plugin, adapter, API, report, or interchange contracts.
Every persisted project envelope must include a schema_version field: a semantic version for this persistence envelope.

Every persisted project envelope must include a project field: project identity, declared unit-system reference, canonical model payload, optional rule-pack references, optional provenance manifest, and a private-data marker.
Every persisted project envelope must include a hash field: canonicalization and checksum metadata for the project payload and hash manifest.
Every persisted project envelope must include a migration field carrying one of: current, stale, unsupported, migrated, failed, newer-than-supported, or TBD migration state.
Optional but expected envelope fields include document_kind, physical_container, round_trip_manifest, and diagnostics.
The validation_profile field records the required validation gates.
The service_operations field records the application-service operation contract for create/open/save/validate/version-check/migrate behavior.
Round-trip serialization first parses the project document.
Round-trip serialization validates the document against the persistence envelope and the delegated model schema.
Round-trip serialization normalizes only schema-approved representation details.
Round-trip serialization serializes JSON payloads using JCS-compatible canonical JSON for hashable payloads.
Round-trip serialization parses the serialized output again.
Round-trip serialization compares semantic equality for model content, unit metadata, loads, rule-pack references, provenance metadata, and reproducibility metadata.

Round-trip checks must preserve engineering-relevant data and must not insert silent defaults for missing units, provenance, rule-pack values, material data, component data, SIF/flexibility inputs, allowables, or load basis values.
Missing solve-required or rule-check-required values are diagnostics.
Volatile/session-only fields may be excluded from deterministic comparison only when the exclusion is documented in the hash or round-trip manifest.
Retrieval sidecars, including SQLite FTS5/BM25 indexes and any later optional NumPy cache, are rebuildable local projections and must be hash-neutral.
External large files are referenced by path or URI plus hash, size, classification, and verification metadata; they are not silently copied into a project package by default.
JSON payload hashes use canonical JSON with JCS-compatible canonicalization.
The schema records canonicalization with hash.canonicalization = "JCS" and checksum entries carrying algorithm, canonicalization, payload_ref, and value.
Hashes must identify what was hashed: project payload, model payload, rule-pack reference metadata, input manifest, report-facing manifest, or external artifact reference.
A hash over environment-local paths, timestamps, UI session state, or other volatile fields is not a reproducibility hash unless the volatile-field treatment is explicitly documented.
Human review records, if added by later work, must bind to specific model, rule-pack, result, and report hashes.
Human review records do not survive content changes and do not imply software certification or automatic code compliance.

The schema records payload scope on checksum records; JSON payload scopes can be classified as project envelope, project payload, model payload, rule-pack reference, input manifest, report manifest, external artifact, state/run records, or result payloads.
Non-JSON and binary artifacts are represented by explicit external artifact references carrying path/URI, hash, size, classification, and verification metadata.
The persistence implementation must diagnose missing, moved, stale, private, or hash-mismatched external files instead of copying them silently or normalizing away the discrepancy.
The persistence envelope records migration state separately from model content.
Migration state 'current' means source and target schema versions match supported persistence behavior.
Migration state 'migration_needed' means the project is stale and requires migration before being treated as current.
Migration state 'migrated' means a migration has produced the target schema version.
Migration state 'unsupported_schema' means the project cannot be opened without a future migration path.
Migration state 'failed' means migration was attempted and failed with diagnostics.
Migration state 'newer_than_supported' means the project was created by a newer schema than this implementation supports.
Migration state 'TBD' means the exact migration state cannot yet be classified.
DB migrations and product schema migrations are separate concerns.
A SQLite store migration may change local tables, indexes, projections, or sidecar metadata without changing the schema-governed canonical project payload.
A product schema migration changes the canonical envelope/model payload contract and must preserve hash evidence and diagnostics.
Unsupported, stale, failed, or newer-than-supported cases must produce structured diagnostics rather than silent coercion.
Private project, material, component, library, and rule-pack data is local-first and user-controlled.
Persistence metadata must mark privacy classification, redistribution status, default transmission permission, quarantine requirements where applicable, and review status.
default_transmission_allowed is false in private-data markers.
Public export, telemetry, repository contribution, issue attachment, or cloud synchronization are separate reviewed actions and are not implied by create/open/save.
If protected or proprietary content is suspected, persistence validation must emit an IP/private-data diagnostic and route the content to quarantine/human review.
Public artifacts for this deliverable must use invented, original, public-domain, or permissively licensed data only.
Persistence operations are application-service boundaries.

Create project accepts project identity, unit-system reference, storage/private-data policy, and optional template reference; returns a versioned envelope or diagnostics and may initialize a local SQLite project store.

Open project accepts a project artifact reference; returns parsed canonical payload, schema/version result, DB migration status, product schema migration status, validation diagnostics, and hash evidence where available.

Save project accepts a validated envelope and target artifact reference; writes canonical JSON/JCS-compatible payload bytes into the local SQLite store and returns hash/manifest evidence plus diagnostics.
Validate project checks schema shape, model schema delegation, unit metadata, provenance, rule-pack references, private-data markers, protected-content boundary, and professional-boundary language.
Version check classifies current, stale, unsupported, failed, newer-than-supported, or TBD migration state.
Migrate project returns a migrated envelope/store state or structured failure diagnostics, with DB migration and product schema migration results recorded separately.

Adapters and plugins may translate import/export formats, but must not open the SQLite store directly, receive raw SQLite handles, issue SQL, depend on table names, or bypass schema validation, unit checks, provenance checks, diagnostics, private-data controls, protected-content screening, or professional-boundary restrictions.
The schema exposes the service contract through PersistenceOperation records.
Each PersistenceOperation declares its application-service boundary, minimum inputs, minimum outputs, diagnostic classes, and bypass_prohibited = true.
The validation profile requires schema validation.
The validation profile requires delegation to schemas/model.schema.yaml for model payload structure.
The validation profile requires unit metadata checks.
The validation profile requires provenance checks.
The validation profile requires rule-pack reference checks.
The validation profile requires protected-content checks.
The validation profile requires private-data checks.
The validation profile requires professional-boundary checks.
The validation profile requires telemetry defaulting to off.

These validation checks are the persistence boundary that prevents SQLite storage, sidecars, adapters, imports, exports, and future project containers from bypassing the OpenPipeStress data and authority constraints.
Persisted projects may carry external human-review or project-acceptance references only as hash-bound records.
Human acceptance records must identify the external acceptance reference, the authority kind, the binding hashes, and invalidates_on_hash_change = true.
Human acceptance references are not solver outputs, rule-pack outputs, certification, sealing, authentication, or automatic code-compliance statuses.
The canonical binding of human acceptance references is the hash-bound project envelope and related payload hashes, even when the bytes are stored inside the local SQLite project store.
Migration rollback semantics and user-facing recovery wording remain to be determined.
